title: Waru waru raised fields, Lake Titicaca basin
summary: Farmers around Lake Titicaca built raised earthen fields, called waru waru, in stages over many generations. Thermoluminescence dating of pottery placed the fields between 1000 BCE and the start of the common era. Penn Museum counts about 82,000 hectares of them, with the largest block near Huatta in Peru.

uncertainty.note: Penn Museum (Erickson, 1988) gives "between 1000 B.C. and the beginning of our era"; ArchDaily says the techniques were developed before 1000 B.C. and the system evolved over at least 2,000 years. The end year is the start plus those 2,000 years, a minimum. The record id says -0500; the sources give -999.

reviewer_note: The record id says -0500 but both sources date the fields to about 1000 BCE onward, so start is -999 and I kept the id. Penn gives fields 4–10 m wide and 10–100 m long; ArchDaily gives 5–10 m and up to 50 m or more, so I cite only Penn's totals. Pin is Huata district centre (the Penn study area is Huatta); the field area covers much of the basin, hence 50 km. Another study dates some fields to about 600 CE, which I did not open.
